name: Google Workspace
summary: Google Workspace OAuth requires configuring a consent screen in the Google Cloud console and creating an OAuth client ID. The main gate is scope verification for sensitive/restricted scopes; start by opening the Google Auth platform in the Cloud console.

oauth_note.text: Supports standard OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with PKCE (plain and S256) and client‑secret flow for web apps; no other grant types are mentioned.

app_types.name: OAuth client ID (Web, Android, iOS, etc.)

registration_access_claim.text: A personal Google account was enough to create a project, the branding/consent configuration and a web OAuth client. The console offers a free trial but nothing required billing.

prerequisites.text: A Google Cloud project linked to the Workspace domain and a logged‑in admin account.

steps.title: Open Google Cloud console
steps.detail: Navigate to Menu → Google Auth platform → Branding (or directly to https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials).

steps.title: Configure OAuth consent screen
steps.detail: Enter App name, support email, select user type (Internal or External), add contact email, and accept the User Data Policy. If External, add test users under Audience.

steps.title: Add required scopes
steps.detail: In the consent screen, click ‘Add scopes’ and select the minimal Google Workspace scopes your app needs. Sensitive/restricted scopes will trigger verification.

steps.title: Create OAuth client ID
steps.detail: In the Cloud console go to Menu → Google Auth platform → Clients, click ‘Create Client’, choose ‘Web application’, give a name, and add authorized redirect URIs (e.g., https://yourapp.com/oauth2/callback).

steps.title: Save client secret
steps.detail: After creation, copy the client ID and client secret; store them securely for your agent to use when building the authorization URL.

steps.title: Test the flow
steps.detail: Use the generated client ID to build an authorization URL, go through consent, and exchange the code at https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token to obtain access/refresh tokens.

approval_claim.text: Verification centre: 'Verification is not required since your app is configured with a testing publishing status.' Audience page: 'Allowed user cap prior to app verification is 100, and is counted over the entire lifetime of the app.' So a new External app starts in Testing, works for listed test users without any review, and verification is the gate for publishing to everyone (and, per Data access, scopes are classed non-sensitive / sensitive / restricted).

unreviewed_limits.text: Publishing status 'Testing': only users added as test users can authorise, and the cap before verification is 100 users over the app's entire lifetime (shown as '0 users (0 test, 0 other) / 100 user cap'). 'Publish app' is greyed out until the Branding configuration is complete.

review_artifacts.text: Privacy policy URL, demo video, justification for each sensitive/restricted scope, and possibly a security assessment.

approval_wait.note: Docs do not specify a timeline for scope verification.

setup_time.note: console.cloud.google.com with a personal Gmail account: create a project, then Google Auth Platform (the renamed 'OAuth consent screen') → Create branding, a 4-step wizard (Project configuration: app name + support email; Audience: Internal/External; Contact information; Finish). Then Clients → Create client → Web application → redirect URI → Create; the client ID and secret appear in a dialog with a 'Download JSON' button. About 13 minutes including project creation; no review at this stage.

redirect_uri_rules.text: The web client form has separate 'Authorised JavaScript origins' and 'Authorised redirect URIs' lists. http://localhost:8000/callback was accepted as a redirect URI. The form warns: 'It may take five minutes to a few hours for settings to take effect', so a freshly added redirect URI can be rejected at first.

token_lifecycle.text: Authorization code exchange returns an access token (typically 1 hour) and a refresh token (long‑lived). Offline access is granted by including access_type=offline. Refresh tokens can be revoked via the console.

scopes_note.text: Scopes are URI strings like https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive. Sensitive scopes need verification; incremental auth is supported via the ‘include_granted_scopes’ parameter.

pkce_required.text: PKCE is supported (plain and S256) but not required for web apps; required for native apps.

blockers.blocker: Using a sensitive or restricted scope without verification
blockers.fix: Submit the verification request with privacy policy and scope justification

blockers.blocker: Missing consent screen configuration (no user type selected)
blockers.fix: Complete the consent screen setup before creating a client ID
Ensure the exact URI used in the auth request is listed in the client ID’s authorized URIs

blockers.blocker: Attempting to create credentials without admin access
blockers.fix: Log in with a Workspace admin or a user with Cloud console permissions

blockers.blocker: Using HTTP (non‑HTTPS) redirect URIs in production
blockers.fix: Switch to HTTPS; only localhost may use HTTP for testing

blockers.blocker: The 'OAuth consent screen' that most docs and tutorials refer to is now 'Google Auth Platform' with Branding / Audience / Clients / Data access / Verification centre pages; menu names in older guides do not match.
blockers.fix: In the console search box type 'Google Auth Platform', or open console.cloud.google.com/auth/overview with your project selected.

blockers.blocker: Internal audience is only for Google Workspace organisations; a personal account must choose External, which starts in Testing mode with a 100-user lifetime cap.
blockers.fix: Add each tester's Google account under Audience → Test users; plan verification before you need more than 100 users.

blockers.blocker: A newly created client or newly added redirect URI may not work immediately.
blockers.fix: Wait; the console states settings can take five minutes to a few hours to take effect.

agent_can: build authorization URL with client ID and scopes
exchange authorization code for tokens via token endpoint
human_must: accept Google API Services User Data Policy

Whether a paid tier is required for external app publishing

tested_notes.text: The Create client form has a checkbox 'Use this client for an AI-powered agent': 'Designates this client for AI agents that take actions on behalf of users. Select this if your client uses Google MCP tools. If your application supports both AI agent workflows and standard user features, use separate OAuth clients for each.' None of the docs the agent read mentioned this.

Audience wizard text for External: 'Your app will start in testing mode and will only be available to users that you add to the list of test users. Once your app is ready to push to production, you may need to verify your app.' Internal: 'You will not need to submit your app for verification.'
Data access page groups scopes into non-sensitive and sensitive ('scopes that request access to private user data'); verification requirements follow from which group you request.
Client credentials can be downloaded as JSON (client_secret.json) from the creation dialog and later from Clients.
Corrects the generated guide: the console's own text confirms the 100-user cap is lifetime, not concurrent, and that verification is tied to publishing status, not to creating the client.

difficulty.label: Hard
reasons: Some scopes need review before real use
